entries.name: The Advisor
entries.concept: A covenant's living memory: an educated custos who knows the Order, its magi and its protocol, and keeps his master out of trouble.
entries.characteristics_advice: Physical Characteristics -1 each; +3, +2, +1 and +1 for the mental ones, Intelligence highest (+2 to Perception for a watchful Advisor, or to Communication for a messenger or herald).

entries.packages: Charmer, Covenfolk, Courtier, Cunning Man, Failed Apprentice (its Penetration xp can go to the Realm Lores instead)
entries.notes: The Virtues are almost essential; the Flaws are open (Tainted with Evil, or Weak Characteristics from years of study).

entries.name: The Almogavars
entries.concept: Light infantry of the Aragonese frontier: javelin, short sword and courage, lightly armored and fast.
entries.packages: Childhood: Athletic, Mischievous or Traveling; Javeliner, Soldier, Woodsman; Forager
entries.notes: Equipment: sheepskin and an open-faced iron helmet (Protection 1, Load 1), a short sword, perhaps a small round shield, and the azcona, a short spear used on foot or mounted or thrown as a javelin. The book's Ability lists don't count any Virtues or Flaws.

entries.name: Animal Trainer
entries.concept: A shepherd, falconer, horse-master or kennel master: anyone whose trade is beasts, mundane or magical.

variants.name: William, age 35, kennel master
variants.flaw_hint: The book gives William Magical Air, a Major Flaw in the Definitive Edition, which a grog can't take: choose Minor Flaws in its place.

entries.packages: Animal Trainer, Farmer, Magician (for magical animals), Rider, Woodsman
entries.notes: Every Animal Trainer needs a good Animal Handling; also Ride for a horseman, Leadership for a master of kennels, Bargain for a dealer, Survival on the moors, Hunt for a falconer, and a Profession for the trade (Feuterer, master of hounds).
fixes: The book gives Madoc "Strong Characteristics", which no book defines; read as Improved Characteristics.
The book gives William Magical Air; in the Definitive Edition it is a Major Flaw, which a grog can't take, so it is left out.
The book names no Social Status for Madoc and Alyse; Covenfolk is offered.

entries.name: Bodyguard Maidservant
entries.concept: A bland, demure maidservant no one notices, who guards her master and can fill many quieter roles.
entries.packages: Childhood: Social, Exploring or Mischievous; Courtier, Conman, Harlot, Tumbler, Servant; Charmer, Covenfolk
entries.notes: Covenfolk keeps her unnoticed (Custos would make her too visible). Warrior lets her learn weapons beyond daggers; Educated or Arcane Lore suit an older one.
fixes: The book suggests Mistaken Identity, a Major Flaw in the Definitive Edition, which a grog can't take; left out.

entries.name: The Bull
entries.concept: The classic big, strong, not-too-bright fighting grog.
entries.flaw_hint: The book also suggests Offensive Fighter, which no book defines: a Minor Personality Flaw is recommended in its place.
entries.packages: Childhood: Athletic, Covenant-bred or Exploring; Footpad, Laborer, Sentry, Soldier; Brawler, Covenfolk, Local
entries.notes: Unless his Social Status lets him learn Martial Abilities, he needs a Virtue for them (Warrior). He is no leader: Custos, Mercenary Captain, Outlaw Leader or Knight don't fit.
fixes: The book suggests Offensive Fighter, which neither Grogs nor the Definitive Edition defines; left out, with a Minor Personality Flaw recommended instead.
The book suggests Outlaw as his Social Status; in the Definitive Edition it is a Major Flaw, which a grog can't take; left out.

entries.name: The Confessor
entries.concept: The covenant's priest, imam or rabbi, who hears the magi's confessions and confronts them with their deeds.

variants.name: Jewish
variants.flaw_hint: The book also gives the Jewish Confessor Outsider, a second Social Status, which a grog can't have: choose another Minor Flaw in its place.

entries.packages: Childhood: Mischievous; Student (parish school), Churchman (at least one package in three); Covenfolk, Local, Leader, Public Official
entries.notes: The Ability lists are for a Christian priest; an imam or rabbi has a different focus and the 50 xp of his Educated Virtue. Uncertain Faith is also a Personality Trait of at least 1.
fixes: The book gives the Jewish Confessor Outsider (Minor) beside Rabbi; a grog has one Social Status, so Outsider is left out.
The book's lists are for a Christian priest; for the Islamic and Jewish Confessors their Theology is of their own faith.

entries.name: The Corpse-Thief
entries.concept: A graveyard robber who sells the bodies of the hanged and the unbaptized to witches and warlocks, and knows the occult worth of what he steals.
entries.packages: Footpad, Apothecary, Magician, Craftsman, Cultist, Local
entries.notes: He needs a Virtue that opens the Arcane Abilities (Arcane Lore). Magic Sensitivity lets him find vis himself; Penetration covers arcane and sympathetic connections.

entries.name: The Craftsman
entries.concept: The covenant's blacksmith (or other craftsman), growing from apprentice to master as the saga goes on.
entries.characteristics_advice: A bias toward the physical Characteristics: Strength for a blacksmith, Dexterity for most other crafts.
entries.packages: Covenfolk, Craftsman, Local, Trader, Trainer (early xp can go to the Realm Lores)
entries.notes: An apprentice starts about 15, is a journeyman by 30 and a master by 45. Custos for a journeyman opens Finesse and Latin. Animal Companion is common.

entries.name: Ex-Prostitute
entries.concept: A woman who has left the trade to make a clean start at the covenant.
entries.packages: Lay Brother (Lay Sister), Laborer, Craftsman, Servant
entries.notes: Virtues tied to her old trade (Gossip, Protection, Social Contacts) are usually lost when she leaves home: take only what she'll use in play.

entries.name: The Failed Apprentice
entries.concept: An apprentice whose Gift deserted him, with nowhere to go but the covenant that knows what he saw.
entries.flaw_hint: In place of Missing Eye, the book suggests a Personality Flaw for his bitterness at losing his Gift.
entries.characteristics_advice: Intelligence and Stamina first; positive Perception or Dexterity.
entries.packages: Covenfolk, Failed Apprentice, Magician, Natural Philosopher, Teacher
entries.notes: The Ability lists don't count Broken Vessel or any Arts learned from his old master.

entries.name: The Farrier
entries.concept: The horses' craftsman: hoof care, shoeing and the horse-doctoring an army or covenant can't do without.
entries.packages: Childhood: Athletic or Social; Craftsman (Craft A Farrier, B Animal Handling or Blacksmith), Farmer, Animal Trainer; Covenfolk, Trainer
entries.notes: Craft: Farrier (General) can stand in for Animal Handling or Medicine to cure a horse, +1 (+3 for the feet).
fixes: The book suggests Vulnerable to Folk Tradition, a Hermetic Flaw in the Definitive Edition, which a grog can't take; left out.

entries.name: Jack-of-All-Trades
entries.concept: A drifter who never held a job long: good at a little of everything, master of nothing.
entries.packages: Many three-year packages, most of them Martial
entries.notes: Take at least one Flaw that explains his drifting (Craving for Travel, Jinxed, Lesser Malediction, Unlucky, Social Handicap or Tainted with Evil), and a Virtue that lets him learn Martial Abilities (the lists need them). No Puissant or Affinity.

entries.name: Misguided Mystic
entries.concept: A seer whose power is real, imagined, or misunderstood, sheltering at the covenant from those who want prophecies or a witch-burning.
entries.packages: Local, Cunning Man, Conman, Mystic, Storyteller
entries.notes: The lists need a Virtue that opens the Arcane Abilities, and include no Supernatural ones: a Supernatural Virtue's Ability comes on top (an older Mystic has the xp). Choose the Realm each power is aligned to.

entries.name: The Murderer
entries.concept: A killer sheltering in the covenant's sanctuary, making himself useful at any menial task.
entries.characteristics_advice: A high Dexterity, and at least positive Strength and Stamina.
entries.packages: Brawler, Covenfolk, Craftsman, Laborer, Local, Servant, Tinker (each over four Abilities, for Master of None)
entries.notes: With Infamous his Local Reputation as a murderer starts at 4.
fixes: The book's Climb (an older edition's Ability) is added to Athletics, which covers climbing in the Definitive Edition.
The book's Fishing (an older edition's Ability) is Profession: Fisherman.

entries.name: Parent of a Gifted Child
entries.concept: A mother or father who followed their Gifted child into the covenant, and now cares for the apprentices.
entries.notes: No combat skills, but they have traveled two regions with the child. The Craft and Profession Abilities are left open for the background.

entries.name: The Refugee Librarian
entries.concept: The librarian of a fallen covenant, come to serve new masters.

entries.packages: Covenfolk, Craftsman (as Bookbinder, Librarian and Scribe), Leader, Trainer
entries.notes: Magic Items: the Librarian's Buckle (ReCo 25, 24 uses a day), the old covenant's badge of office, lets him move freely through the air.

entries.name: The Role-Bound Ferryman
entries.concept: The only one who knows the way across the marsh to the covenant, bound to his role by a supernatural curse.
entries.characteristics_advice: A poor Communication and a high Stamina.
entries.packages: Athletic childhood; then his own three-year packages: Covenfolk (+5 Area Lore, +20 Covenant Lore, +15 Craft: Boatbuilder, +5 Order of Hermes Lore), Local, Magician, Sailor, Scout
entries.notes: A role-bound grog needs a Profession or Craft that defines him. By 65 he has an enriched Item of Virtue from the Magician package.

entries.name: The Street Thug
entries.concept: A city brawler with contacts on both sides of the law, who sides with the magi for money and protection.
entries.packages: Brawler, Footpad (its Legerdemain xp to Thrown Weapon), Leader, Local, Soldier, Wastrel
entries.notes: Puissant Brawl and Tough can give way to Berserk, Large or Enduring Constitution; an older thug may swap a Flaw for Infamous (a bad Reputation of 4). Poor Living Conditions ages him fast.
fixes: The book's Climb (an older edition's Ability) is added to Athletics, which covers climbing in the Definitive Edition.
The book's Disguise (an older edition's Ability) is added to Guile.

entries.name: Time-Lost Witness
entries.concept: Someone lost in Faerie for centuries, returned to a world that has moved on: here, a Roman legionary.
entries.notes: The example is a Roman legionary lost in a faerie wood, who re-emerges in 1220: Worthless Abilities covers his Organization Lore: Roman Army.
fixes: A legionary's Latin is his native, living language (Living Language: Latin).
